business_problem: MISA needed to move from expensive, externally hosted LLM APIs to a self-hosted Vietnamese AI stack that could protect sensitive data, reduce latency and operating cost, and support many concurrent public-service and enterprise automation workloads.
solution_summary: MISA built an on-premises AI factory on NVIDIA infrastructure so it could own the full lifecycle of Vietnamese domain models and AI agents. The core cluster uses eight NVIDIA DGX H200 systems linked with NVIDIA Quantum InfiniBand networking, while NVIDIA A40 GPUs handle smaller specialized tasks such as eKYC and router LLMs. NVIDIA Run:ai virtualizes the cluster and enables fractional GPU sharing, which increased concurrent experimentation dramatically. On top of that hardware, MISA uses NVIDIA NeMo for domain-specific tuning, NVIDIA Dynamo and NVIDIA NIM for production-scale serving, and FP8 quantization to raise inference throughput for real-time agent interactions. The AI factory powers more than 50 prebuilt agents and hundreds of templates, including MISA AVA, MISA AMIS OneAI, Support, Mail, and Recruitment assistants, so accounting, tax, HR, sales, and public-administration workflows can run securely on self-hosted infrastructure instead of external APIs.

data_flow: Business and public-service data enter MISA’s self-hosted AI factory, DGX H200 clusters and NeMo fine-tune domain models, Dynamo and NIM serve those models to AVA and other agents, and the outputs automate accounting, HR, sales, support, and public-administration tasks inside customer workflows.
business_outcome: MISA cut fine-tuning time by 4x, increased throughput from 1,200 to 4,500 TPS per model, saved about $200,000 per month, automated recruiting workflows in minutes with up to 90 percent HR time savings, and now uses the platform to support more than 450,000 organizations and over 1.1 million daily LLM requests.
